simple: A `Beam` draws a picture stretched between two attachments, like a laser, rope of light, waterfall, or force field. You can color it, fade it, make it wider at one end, and even bend it into a curve. Beams are one of the easiest ways to make cool sci-fi or magic effects. The two attachments decide where it starts and ends.
analogy: It is like a ribbon tied between two hooks: move the hooks and the ribbon moves with them, and you can choose the ribbon's pattern, color, and how wide each end is.
keyPoints: A beam needs two attachments: `Attachment0` is the start and `Attachment1` is the end. Remove one and the beam disappears.
To build one: put an attachment in each of two parts, insert a Beam, then set its `Attachment0` and `Attachment1` properties.
`Texture` sets the picture, `Color` tints it (one color or a gradient), and `Transparency` can fade it along its length.
`Width0` and `Width1` set how wide each end is in studs. Values below 0 are reset to 0.
`TextureLength` and `TextureMode` decide how often the texture repeats along the beam.
`FaceCamera = true` keeps the flat beam turned toward the camera so it does not vanish when seen from the side.
Beams can curve. `CurveSize0` and `CurveSize1` bend it, using each attachment's facing direction.
Turn on Show Constraint Details in the View menu to see attachments while building.

terms.attachment: An invisible point in a part that marks where something connects. Beams start at one attachment and end at another.
terms.texture: The image drawn along the beam, like a striped laser pattern.
terms.ColorSequence: A color gradient. A beam can go from blue at the start to purple at the end.
terms.NumberSequence: A list of numbers that change along the beam, used to fade transparency from 0 at one end to 1 at the other.
terms.opaque / transparent: Opaque (0) means you cannot see through it; fully transparent (1) means invisible.
terms.Width0 / Width1: How wide the beam is at the start and at the end. Width0 = 0.5 and Width1 = 3 makes it flare out like a cone.
terms.TextureMode: How the image repeats. With Wrap or Static, a 20-stud beam with TextureLength 4 repeats the image 5 times. With Stretch, it repeats exactly TextureLength times.
terms.segments: The little pieces a beam is split into so it can bend smoothly. More segments make a smoother curve.
terms.Bezier curve: A smooth curve shaped by control points. The beam bends toward points that sit `CurveSize0` studs out from the start and `CurveSize1` studs out from the end.
terms.2D projection: Something flat drawn in a 3D world. Seen exactly edge-on, it can look invisible.

example.title: Draw a glowing laser between two parts
example.place: Script in ServerScriptService (with two parts named LaserStart and LaserEnd in Workspace)
example.code:
local startPart = workspace:WaitForChild("LaserStart")
local endPart = workspace:WaitForChild("LaserEnd")

local attach0 = Instance.new("Attachment")
attach0.Parent = startPart
local attach1 = Instance.new("Attachment")
attach1.Parent = endPart

local beam = Instance.new("Beam")
beam.Attachment0 = attach0
beam.Attachment1 = attach1
beam.Color = ColorSequence.new(Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0))
beam.Width0 = 0.3
beam.Width1 = 0.3
beam.FaceCamera = true -- always visible from any angle
beam.LightEmission = 1 -- glow
beam.Parent = startPart
explain: We find the two parts and add an attachment to each one.
We create a `Beam` and tell it which attachment is the start and which is the end.
We make it red and 0.3 studs wide at both ends.
`FaceCamera` keeps it from disappearing when viewed from the side.
Parenting it into the game makes it show up. Move either part and the beam follows.

watchOut: Setting both attachments to the same attachment draws nothing. They must be two different attachments.
If your beam vanishes at certain angles, turn on `FaceCamera`.
A beam that is unexpectedly curved probably has nonzero `CurveSize0` or `CurveSize1`. Set them to 0 for a straight line.
A beam is just a picture. It does not block or hurt players unless you script that.
